forms.label: Dried
forms.sourceNote: USDA has no record for barberries (Berberis vulgaris/integerrima), and no regional or national food-composition table for them could be found that was accessible to read directly, so a stand-in is used. USDA's raw-cranberry record (a wrong water content: raw fruit cited for a dried one) was replaced with dried, unsweetened Zante currants — a small dried fruit at a comparable water content to dried barberries, rather than a fresh fruit understating the energy and mineral concentration several-fold. Zante currants are sweeter and less acidic than barberries, so this is still an approximation, not a match.
forms.nutritionCaveat: Cited against dried Zante currants because USDA carries no barberry record and no unsweetened dried-cranberry record either. The water content is a reasonable match for a dried fruit, but Zante currants are a sweeter, less tart fruit than barberries, so the sugar figure in particular likely overstates barberries and the true profile is closer to a tart, low-sugar dried fruit than this record shows.
